title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is not a manuscript page. It is a typed page, page 35 of SGA 7, Exposé IX (Grothendieck, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie'), photographed upside down. The sheet was evidently reused as scratch paper; the 1976 handwritten notes on the neighbouring pages (coalgebras S, C, the functor V, the cotensor product C ⊠_S C', P = Ker(C⊗C' ⇉ C⊗C'⊗S)) are on other sides/pages.

The typed mathematics is the semistable reduction theory for abelian varieties. A_K is an abelian variety over the fraction field K of a henselian DVR. I is the inertia group, π the Galois group, and T_ℓ the Tate module, with ℓ different from the residue characteristic.

1. The page first gives the canonical π-equivariant isomorphism (*): H^1(A_{K̄}, Z_ℓ) ≅ Hom(T_ℓ(A(K̄)), Z_ℓ). By this duality, assertion 3.7 (an open subgroup of I acts on T_ℓ with unipotence échelon 2, i.e. potential semistable reduction) reduces to the corresponding statement on H^1. That statement is cited as proved in an earlier exposé of SGA 7, via resolution of singularities of excellent 2-dimensional schemes. This is Grothendieck's geometric proof of the ℓ-adic monodromy theorem.

2. Corollary 3.8 adds a further condition to the equivalent conditions of 3.5 (semistable reduction, etc.): (vi) I acts unipotently on T_ℓ.
   - Proof that (v) implies (vi): suppose I acts unipotently on a finite-dimensional Q_ℓ-space E, and a finite-index subgroup I' acts with échelon m (here m = 2).
   - The Zariski closures G' ⊂ G ⊂ GL(E) satisfy [G : G'] < ∞.
   - G is unipotent, hence connected in characteristic 0, so G = G'.
   - Therefore I and I' have the same unipotence échelon.

3. Corollary 3.9 begins a converse to 3.3: semistable reduction is characterised by a condition on Néron models under every étale extension K'/K, namely the canonical morphism A ⊗_S S' → A'. The page breaks off at this point.
errors: No mathematical errors. The argument is correct, since the unipotence échelon of a group is determined by its Zariski closure.

The 'III' in the cross-reference may be a mis-rendering. The geometric proof of the monodromy theorem using 2-dimensional resolution is in SGA 7 Exposé I; the typed text may have a blank or an 'I' there. This could not be verified with certainty from the image.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a reused typed page of the published SGA 7 Exposé IX, photographed upside down. Its content is fully published and credited. The actual 1976 notes (coalgebra cotensor products) are on the neighbouring pages, not here.
transcription_corrections: The page image is upside down. It is a typescript of SGA 7 Exposé IX, p. 35, not a manuscript note.
'prouvée dans III' is possibly 'prouvée dans I' followed by a blank space left for a reference. SGA 7 Exposé I contains the geometric monodromy proof.
The handwritten numbers '353' (archive stamp) and '282' are archival foliation marks, not content.
